usageNotes: Use this to inspect the full definition of a specific custom CPU model before assigning it to a VM — confirming its reported-model, enabled/disabled flags, and any phys-bits or level overrides. The caller must hold Mapping.Audit, Mapping.Use, or Mapping.Modify on the path /mapping/cpu/{cputype}. The 'custom-' prefix in the cputype path segment is optional; the API normalises both forms.

examples.summary: Retrieve details for a custom CPU model named 'custom-secure-epyc'

tips: Custom CPU model names are defined cluster-wide in /etc/pve/cpu-models.conf; verify the model exists there before querying.
The returned 'digest' field can be passed to modification calls to guard against concurrent edits.
Using 'phys-bits: host' in a custom model breaks live migration between hosts with different physical address bit widths — check this field before migrating VMs that use the model.
If the response 'hidden' flag is true, the guest OS will not detect it is running inside KVM, which is useful for software that refuses to run in virtual environments.
